env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The agent can search your codebase to find relevant context, but providing it explicitly improves response quality and reduces latency.
env_context_strategy.note: User @-mentions add explicit context; default is agent search.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Compaction summarizes earlier messages and replaces them in the model context with that summary
context_compaction.evidence_locator: paper Sec. Token Usage and Compaction

observation_format.evidence_quote: It’s also possible to attach images in your prompt for providers that support vision models.
observation_format.note: Images are user-supplied context; tool results are text.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: Tool calling needs to be individually supported by each model and model provider.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: You can add external tools with MCP Servers.
tool_schema_source.evidence_locator: paper Sec. Using Tools and Profiles
tool_schema_source.note: Built-in tool schema source not reported.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Use External Agents for ACP-integrated agents.
protocol_standardization.note: other = Agent Client Protocol (ACP); MCP servers also supported.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: Responses stream in with indicators showing which tools the model is using.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: By default, the Agent Panel uses Zed’s first-party agent.
multi_agent_topology.note: Multiple threads run independently, not delegated.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: You can run multiple agent threads at once, each working independently with its own agent, context window, and conversation history.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: Use Tool Permissions to control whether permission-gated tool calls are allowed, denied, or confirmed.
human_in_loop.evidence_locator: paper Sec. Using Tools and Profiles
human_in_loop.note: Also human review of diffs at completion.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: each working independently with its own agent, context window, and conversation history

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: You can mention files, directories, symbols, previous threads, skills, diagnostics, branch diffs, and URLs to fetch.
long_term_memory.note: Skills and past threads are mentionable across runs.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: The Thread History holds all your threads across all projects, sorted chronologically, and you can restore them at any time.

self_verification.evidence_quote: You can accept or reject each individual change hunk, or the whole set of changes made by the agent.
self_verification.note: Review is human, not harness-enforced verification; no automated tests/linters described.

rollback.evidence_quote: Every time the model performs an edit, you should see a “Restore Checkpoint” button at the top of your message, allowing you to return your code base to the state it was in prior to that message.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: a banner appears above the message editor as you approach the token limit
termination_condition.evidence_locator: paper Sec. Token Usage and Compaction
termination_condition.note: Model finishing generation ends the turn; user can also interrupt.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: The same model can be offered via multiple providers - for example, Claude Sonnet 4.5 is available via Zed Pro, OpenRouter, Anthropic directly, and more.
cost_controls.note: User-selected model/provider; no token budget or caching documented.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: The Agent Panel is where you interact with AI agents that can read, write, and run code in your project.
execution_isolation.note: Runs in the local editor on the user's project; git worktree isolation optional.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: If two threads might edit the same files, you can isolate one in a new Git worktree.

network_policy.evidence_quote: You can mention files, directories, symbols, previous threads, skills, diagnostics, branch diffs, and URLs to fetch.
network_policy.note: No network restriction documented; URL fetching supported.

permission_model.evidence_quote: Use Tool Permissions to control whether permission-gated tool calls are allowed, denied, or confirmed.
permission_model.evidence_locator: paper Sec. Using Tools and Profiles
permission_model.note: Also profiles restricting which tools are available (static allowlist).

tracing.evidence_quote: open the thread as Markdown with agent: open active thread as markdown and attach it to your GitHub issue
tracing.note: Threads are stored and exportable; format documented only as Markdown.

replayability.evidence_quote: Restoring threads from history, checkpoints, token usage display, and similar features depend on the agent integration.
replayability.note: Threads can be restored/viewed but no replay of actions documented.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: You can rate agent responses to help improve Zed’s system prompt and tools.
eval_hooks.note: Only human feedback ratings; no benchmark evaluation runner documented.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Use Tool Permissions to control whether permission-gated tool calls are allowed, denied, or confirmed.
guardrails.evidence_locator: paper Sec. Using Tools and Profiles

target_domain.evidence_quote: use it for code generation, refactoring, debugging, documentation, and general questions

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: you can switch between their models by clicking on the model selector on the message editor

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: Zed includes built-in tools for searching your codebase, editing files, running terminal commands, and more.
primary_artifact.evidence_locator: paper Sec. Using Tools and Profiles
primary_artifact.note: Coded from product documentation; no paper exists.
